extracted.intended_audience: executive departments and agencies, OIRA and OMB officials, regulatory drafters, and stakeholders in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements from Executive Order 14094 for modernizing federal regulatory review, public participation, OIRA meeting practices, and regulatory analysis. Applies to federal agencies, OIRA/OMB, and parties engaging in notice-and-comment and regulatory planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action (amended definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "(f) \"Significant regulatory action\" means any regulatory action that is likely to result in a rule that may:"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) "have an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more (adjusted every 3 years by the Administrator of OIRA for changes in gross domestic product); or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector of the economy, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State, local, territorial, or tribal governments or communities;" (2) "create a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with an action taken or planned by another agency;" (3) "materially alter the budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights and obligations of recipients thereof;" (4) "raise legal or policy issues for which centralized review would meaningfully further the President's priorities or the principles set forth in this Executive order, as specifically authorized in a timely manner by the Administrator of OIRA in each case."

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative promotion of inclusive regulatory policy and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory actions should be informed by input from a wide set of stakeholders and public groups, and opportunities for public participation should promote equitable and meaningful participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should, to the extent practicable and consistent with law, solicit input from: interested or affected communities; State, local, territorial, and Tribal officials and agencies; interested or affected private-sector parties and regulated entities; those with expertise in relevant disciplines; and the public as a whole. Participation opportunities shall be designed to promote equitable and meaningful participation by a range of interested or affected parties, including underserved communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition clarity, response, and tracking (5 U.S.C. 553(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall clarify opportunities to petition for issuance/amendment/repeal of rules, endeavor to respond efficiently, and maintain/share logs of petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, agencies shall: (i) clarify opportunities for interested persons to petition under 5 U.S.C. 553(e); (ii) endeavor to respond to such petitions efficiently, in light of agency judgments of available resources and priorities; and (iii) maintain, subject to available resources, a log of such petitions received, and share with the Administrator of OIRA, upon request, information on the status of recently resolved and pending petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive engagement to inform regulatory agendas and plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall endeavor to proactively engage interested or affected parties when developing regulatory agendas and plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should include members of underserved communities; consumers; workers and labor organizations; program beneficiaries; businesses and regulated entities; those with expertise in relevant disciplines; and other interested parties. Efforts should incorporate best practices for information accessibility and engagement, including community-based outreach; outreach to organizations that work with interested parties; use of agency field offices; use of alternative platforms and media for engaging the public; and expansion of public capacity for engaging in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize notice-and-comment: guidance and tools for mass/computer-generated/falsely attributed comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator of OIRA, in consultation with relevant agencies, shall consider guidance or tools to modernize the notice-and-comment process, including through technological changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms and guidance may include ways to address mass comments, computer-generated comments (such as those generated through artificial intelligence), and falsely attributed comments, and other technological changes that affect how public input is collected, filtered, and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA meeting access, efficiency, consolidation, and transparency reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect public trust and reduce risk or appearance of undue influence, OIRA shall implement reforms to meeting-request procedures and disclosure practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator of OIRA shall: (i) provide information to facilitate initiation of meeting requests from potential participants not historically requesting such meetings (including underserved communities); and (ii) implement reforms that may include: (A) efforts to ensure access for meeting requesters who have not historically requested such meetings; (B) discouraging meeting requests that are duplicative of earlier meetings with OIRA regarding the same regulatory action by the same requesters; (C) consolidation of meetings by requester, subject matter, or other consistently applied factors to improve efficiency and effectiveness; and (D) disclosure of data in an open, machine-readable, and accessible format that includes the dates and names of individuals involved in all substantive meetings and the subject matter discussed, as required by EO 12866 section 6(b)(4)(C)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analysis should consider distributive impacts and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory analysis should facilitate development of regulations that serve the public interest, advance statutory objectives, and be consistent with EOs 12866 and 13563; analyses shall, as practicable and appropriate, recognize distributive impacts and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs that regulatory analysis, as practicable and appropriate, shall recognize distributive impacts and equity to the extent permitted by law, aligning regulatory analysis with specified executive orders and the Presidential Memorandum of January 20, 2021 (Modernizing Regulatory Review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of OMB Circular A-4 to implement equity/distributive-impact policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year, OMB (through OIRA and with consultation) shall issue revisions to Circular A-4 to implement the policy that regulatory analysis recognize distributive impacts and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of OMB, through the Administrator of OIRA and in consultation with the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers and representatives of relevant agencies, shall issue revisions to the Office of Management and Budget's Circular A-4 of September 17, 2003 (Regulatory Analysis) to implement the policy set forth in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and implementation constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The order does not impair agency legal authority, substitute for law, or create enforceable private rights, and must be implemented consistent with applicable law and available appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General provisions specify: (a)(i) nothing in the order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect authority granted by law to an executive department or agency or its head; (a)(ii) nothing shall affect the functions of the Director of OMB relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; (b) implementation is subject to applicable law and availability of appropriations; and (c) the order does not create any right or benefit enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States or its entities or personnel.
